# Centralizing Literature

![](./fig/rss-overview.svg)

## RSS is a web-based aggregation tool

### Background

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="50%"}
- What does RSS stand for?
    
    - Conflicting accounts!
      - **[R]{.underline}**eally **[S]{.underline}**imple **[S]{.underline}**yndication
      - **[R]{.underline}**ich **[S]{.underline}**ite **[S]{.underline}**ummary
      - **[R]{.underline}**DF **[S]{.underline}**ite **[S]{.underline}**ummary
    - RSS $\equiv$ a website feed aggregator
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
- What ***is*** RSS though?
    
    - Set of technical standards
      - A standard, computer-readable format
    - Written in extensible mark-up language (XML)
    - For storing and sending data through the internet
::::

:::

[**An updating scientific journal website aggregation system!**]{.fragment}


## [An RSS aggregator will centralize all feeds across devices]{style="font-size:0.70em;"}

### Background

The day an important article is published you will be able to find it!

- Single concentrated reference point
  - Track **many** different websites
  - Regular updates (~1-6hrs)
  - Convenient 
    - Desktop
    - Mobile
    - Tablet
    - Browser

## [Too many software options!!!]{style="font-size:0.80em;"}

### Background

::: {.notes}

The goal is not to become a poweruser!!!

This serves a focused purpose and it does that well.

:::

[There are dozens of notable RSS readers.](https://play.google.com/store/search?q=rss+feed+app){target="_blank"}

[Most have a pay-tiered system.]{.fragment}

- I suggest Inoreader... currently
  
  - Most useful options at unpaid subscription level are:
    - Compatible with IOS, Andriod, and the Web
    - Organizing with folders and tags 
    - Highlighting keywords 
    - Ability to search

### Install and Set Up

::: notes

go to science.com and scroll to the bottom

click the rss symbol

copy url of rss xml site and paste into inoreader

wsj:thejournal (rss symbol)

Use nature (rss feed), science (rss symbol), and biorxiv (specific set up) as examples

:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
document.getElementById("userInput").addEventListener("input", function() {
  let userInput = this.value;
  let words = userInput.split("-");
  
  let output = "";
  words.forEach(word => {
    output += `<li>${word}</li>`;
  });
  
  document.getElementById("outputText").innerHTML = `<ul>${output}</ul>`;
});
```

## Make your folders for your feeds

### Install and Set Up

::: columns
::: {.column width="75%"}
-   Consider grouping journals categories:

    -   Broad 
        - interdisciplinary, high-impact factor
    -   Topics 
        - Molecular Biology, Genetics, Bioinformatics 
    -   Time span they publish or you want to check
        - Continuous, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually
        - ["Nature is a weekly international journal"](https://www.nature.com/nature/journal-information){target="_blank"}
    -   Access
        - Open access, Publisher, Preprints
:::

### Suggested Usage


::: columns
::: {.column width="75%"}
Below are some suggestions to speed-up your usage:

-   `n`, `p` or with `shift`: navigate the articles or side-bar
-   `j`, `k` : navigate the Article view or `space`: to scroll through the abstract
-   `m`, `f`: mark the articles as read or read later
-   `1`, `3`: change views from list to cards
-   use `v` to load a new tab or `w` to load the content

## Search the feeds for rapid re/discovery

### Suggested Usage

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
Located at:

-   Upper right [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} :mag:
-   Left-hand [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} :mag:
-   `Add feed` [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Monitor feed`
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Straight-forward operation:

-   Search articles in feeds, folder, or tags

:::: {.fragment}

::::: {.nonincremental}

-   Use boolean operators
    -   `AND`
    -   `OR`
    -   `NOT`
    -   `""`
    -   `()`

:::::

::::    

:::
:::

::: notes
Boolean operators are terms used to combine or exclude keywords in search queries to narrow down or broaden search results in a search engine. They are words like "AND," "OR," and "NOT" that help refine the search by specifying relationships between keywords.

```         
AND: Narrows down the search by requiring both terms to be present in the results. For example, searching for "cats AND dogs" will return results that mention both cats and dogs.

OR: Broadens the search, returning results that include either one or both of the specified terms. Searching for "cats OR dogs" will retrieve results mentioning either cats or dogs or both.

NOT: Excludes specific terms from the search results. For instance, searching for "cats NOT dogs" will display results related to cats but exclude any that mention dogs.
```

These operators are useful for making searches more precise and tailored to your needs by including, excluding, or combining keywords in various ways.
:::

## [ZotMoov allows automated attachment management!]{.small} {.scrollable}

### Install & Setup

::: {.small}

1. `Directory to Move/Copy Files To` should be ***your library directory***
2. `File Behavior` change to `Copy`
3. [Set up your directory structure:](https://github.com/wileyyugioh/zotmoov/blob/master/docs/WILDCARD_INFO.md#zotmoov-wildcard-formatting){target="_blank"}
    - Nested [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow}\n`{/%y}{/%F}`<br>for `~/Year/First_Author`<br>(e.g. `~/2014/ZutJ`)
    - Flattened [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `/{%y}_{%a}`<br>for `~/Year_AuthorLastName`<br>(e.g. `~/2014_Zut`)

[![](./fig/settings-zotmoov.png){.lightbox}]{.fragment .absolute bottom=0 right=0 width=575}

:::

## [A simple, standard directory structure is easy to organize]{.small}

### Suggested Usage

::: columns
::: column
-   PARA
    -   Projects
        -   Short-term efforts
    -   Areas
        -   Long-term efforts
    -   Resources
        -   Topics of interest
    -   Archives
        -   Inactive items from the other categories
:::

::: column
::: vscroll
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| fig-height: 6.5
//| fig-width: 3
digraph PARA { 
  edge [arrowhead=none];
  ranksep=0.5;
  nodesep = 1;
  splines = ortho;
  rankdir = LR;

  node [ shape="folder", width = 1.25, height = 0.75, fixedsize=true, style="filled" gradientangle="270", fillcolor="lightyellow:sandybrown", fontcolor="black"];
  "My Library" [shape="box3d", style="filled" gradientangle="270", fillcolor="sandybrown:peru", fontcolor="black"];
  Projects Areas Resources Archives;

#  node [ shape="note", width = 1, height = 0.5, fixedsize=true, style="filled", fillcolor="white", fontcolor="black"];
#item item2 paper;

  node [ shape="point", width = 0, height = 0];
  { rank = same; W0 W1 W2 W3}

  W0 -> "My Library" [constraint=false];
  W0 -> W1 -> W2 -> W3;        /* critical! */
  
  W0 -> Projects;

  W1 -> Areas;

  W2 -> Resources;

  W3 -> Archives;

    node [ shape="point", width = 0, height = 0 ];
  { rank = same; W0 W3 W2 W1 }
  
}
```
:::
:::
:::

## [A simple, standard directory structure is easy to organize]{.small}

### Suggested Usage

::: columns
::: {.column .nonincremental}
-   PARA
    -   Projects
        -   Short-term efforts
    -   Areas
        -   Long-term efforts
    -   Resources
        -   Topics of interest
    -   Archives
        -   Inactive items from the other categories
:::

::: column
::: vscroll
```{dot}
//| echo: false
//| fig-height: 16.5
//| fig-width: 4.5
digraph PARA { 
  edge [arrowhead=none];
  ranksep=0.5;
  nodesep = 1;
  splines = ortho;
  rankdir = LR;

  node [ shape="folder", width = 1.25, height = 0.75, fixedsize=true, style="filled" gradientangle="270", fillcolor="lightyellow:sandybrown", fontcolor="black"];
  "My Library" [shape="box3d", style="filled" gradientangle="270", fillcolor="sandybrown:peru", fontcolor="black"];
  Projects Areas Resources Archives QE Dissertation "Review\nPaper" Writing "Teaching" "Broader\nImpacts" "Dry\nLab" "Wet\nLab" Learning "Completed\nProjects" "Inactive\nAreas" "Irrelevant\nResources";

#  node [ shape="note", width = 1, height = 0.5, fixedsize=true, style="filled", fillcolor="white", fontcolor="black"];
#item item2 paper;

  node [ shape="point", width = 0, height = 0];
  { rank = same; W0 W1 W2 W3}

  node [ shape="point", width = 0, height = 0];
  { rank = same; P0 P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 P7 P8 P9 P10 P11};

  W0 -> "My Library" [constraint=false];
  W0 -> W1 -> W2 -> W3;        /* critical! */
  
  W0 -> Projects;
  Projects -> P2;
  P0 -> P1 -> P2;
  P0 -> "QE";
  P1 -> "Dissertation";
  P2 -> "Review\nPaper";
  
  W1 -> Areas;
  Areas -> P4;
  P3 -> P4 -> P5;
  P3 -> "Writing";
  P4 -> "Teaching";
  P5 -> "Broader\nImpacts";
  
  W2 -> Resources;
  Resources -> P7;
  P6 -> P7 -> P8;
  P6 -> "Dry\nLab";
  P7 -> "Wet\nLab";
  P8 -> "Learning";
  
  W3 -> Archives;
  Archives -> P9;
  P9 -> P10 -> P11;
  P9 -> "Completed\nProjects";
  P10 -> "Inactive\nAreas";
  P11 -> "Irrelevant\nResources"
  
    node [ shape="point", width = 0, height = 0 ];
  { rank = same; W4 W5 W6 W0 W3 W2 W1 }
  
}
```

## Including headers can increase note organization

### Suggested Usage

::: columns
::: column
Including the `Notes` column for quick reference:

-   Right-click column headers in any collection
-   Check `Notes`
:::

::: column
Quick example of note taking and importing into text editor:

-   Open pdf in Zotero
-   Create annotations (`Alt+1` & `Alt+3`)
-   Right-click item and `Add Note from Annotations`
-   Open text editor
-   Import note
:::
:::

## [Tags are incredible for organizing with visual aids!]{.small}

### Suggested Usage

Use tags to mark all read and unread items:

1.  Add :o: to an item in the `Tags` panel.
2.  In the lower left panel, right click the tag [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Assign Color...`
3.  Select a color and `Set color`
4.  Select all items and drop into the tag

For automatic tagging, install the [Actions and Tags](https://github.com/windingwind/zotero-actions-tags){target="_blank"} addon

## [For increased resolution create a ***Folksonomy***, a thesaurus of tags]{style="font-size: 0.70em;"}

### Suggested Usage

::: columns
::: column
Why?

-   Individuals or groups will quickly find and re-find sources
-   Metadata is shared in groups
    -   Offers guidance to beginners
:::

::: column
How?

-   Think and create some keywords that capture the text contents
-   Skim abstracts and papers for keywords
-   Use bibliometrics or LLMs:
    -   [`Create a folksonomy, or a thesaurus of tags, for [topics] studies.`]{.small}
:::
:::

## [Auto-Curate your library through saved searches]{.small}

### Suggested Usage

::: notes
A final organizational tool within Zotero is the saved searched. By creating curated searches new items will auto populate by well-defined rules set by the user. These saved searches allow a user to find the new items in both their Unfiled collection and their saved searches. All to allow the user more focused options when beginning their reading or writing tasks.
:::

-   Start an advanced search:
    -   Click the :mag:
    -   Click `Edit` [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Advanced Search`
    -   `Ctrl+Shift+F`
-   Define an area of continued interest
-   Using keywords in `All fields`, rapidly tag groups of items

## Citing and bibliographies are simplified

### Suggested Usage

::: notes
Paste the citations: `Ctrl+Shift+C` a Zotero item/s you have selected [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Ctrl+v` in text editor
:::

::: small
-   Google Docs for collabratory documents
    -   Open google doc: Open a google doc in the google drive you would like to sync to your Zotero library.
    -   Link account: Integrate your google account with Zotero by clicking `Z` in the toolbar.
        -   Authenticate the Google account used to edit the document
-   Microsoft Word for local documents
    -   Open Word Doc: Open a word document...
    -   Done?: There is now a Zotero tab in you document linked to your library!
-   Libre Office for local documents
    -   Open Libre Writer: Open a writer document...
    -   Done?: There is now a Zotero toolbar in you document linked to your library!
:::

## [Bibliometrics provides an accessible framework for equitable scholarship]{.smaller}

### Background

["\[Bibliometrics is\] The measurement of all aspects related to the publication and reading of books and documents."](https://www.nature.com/articles/510218e){target="_blank"}

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   [Bibliometrics uses]{.fragment}

    -   Archival database
    -   Article metadata
    -   Statistical analysis
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
-   [Bibliometrics answers]{.fragment}

    -   where the field has grown from

## [Wildcards allow the capture of many individual words]{style="font-size:0.80em;"}

### Databases

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}
| Wildcard Charater | Definition                                | Example | Result                                           |
|:-----------------:|:-----------------|:-----------------:|:-----------------|
|        \*         | Any amount of character/s to include zero | `*man`  | `man, woman, human, superman, superwoman, {etc}` |
|         ?         | Any single character                      | `wom?n` | `woman, women`                                   |
|   \$ (WoS only)   | Any single or no character                | `$$man` | `woman, man, human`                              |

: Wildcards {#tbl-wd}
:::

## [Boolean operators are vital to focus a corpus]{style="font-size:0.80em;"}

### Databases

::: vscroll
::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}
|     Operator      | Affect on Search | Definition                                                                           | Example                               |
|:------------------:|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
|      **AND**      | Narrows          | Intersects *all* terms separated by operator                                               | `migration AND butterfl*`            |
|      **OR**       | Broadens         | Unites *any* and *all* terms separated by operator                                     | `migration OR butterfl*`             |
|      **NOT**      | Narrows          | Excludes term following operator                                                     | `migration AND bird* NOT butterfl*` |
|  **NEAR/x**(WoS)  | Narrows          | Find terms joined by operator *near* each other by $x$ words                         | `America NEAR/10 butterfly`           |
|   **SAME**(WoS)   | Narrows          | Find terms joined by operator if in the *same* sentence                              | `America SAME butterfly`              |
|  **W/n**(Scopus)  | Narrows          | Find terms joined by operator *within* each other by $n$ words                       | `American W/10 butterfly`             |
| **Pre/n**(Scopus) | Narrows          | Find terms where *preceeding* term to operator is within $n$ words of following term | `American Pre/3 butterfly`            |

: Boolean Operators {#tbl-bo}
:::
:::

## Searching by phrase may simplify a search

### Databases

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}
|    Phrase type    |       Example        |                       Search                       |
|:----------------------:|:----------------------:|:----------------------:|
|     **Loose**     | `"phrase searching"` | `phrase search, phrase searches, phrase searching` |
| **Exact**(Scopus) | `{phrase searching}` |                 `phrase searching`                 |

: Pharse Searching {#tbl-ps}
:::

::: notes
lemmatization and stemming (i.e. techniques to reduce words to their root form)

loose allows for wildcards to be included in the quotations. exact will search for the exact characters inbetween the curly braces (do not include wildcards)
:::

## [Combine all search techniques for the best corpus results]{.small} {auto-animate="true"}

### Databases

WoS = 184

::: {.smaller data-id="wos"}
> ALL=(("colorectal cancer\*" OR "colorectal neoplas\*" OR "adenomatous polyposis coli" OR "colon\* neoplas\*" OR "rectal neoplas\*" OR "hereditary nonpolypo\*") AND ("metagenom\*" AND "metabol\*"))
:::

Scopus = 367 & PubMed = 248

::: {.smaller data-id="scopus"}
> TITLE-ABS-KEY ( "colorectal cancer\*" OR "colorectal neoplas\*" OR "adenomatous polyposis coli" OR "colon\* neoplas\*" OR "rectal neoplas\*" OR "hereditary nonpolypo\*" AND "metagenom\*" AND "metabol\*" )
:::

## Achievable goals lead to accomplishments

### Techniques for Success

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="35%"}

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false

    }
}}%%

flowchart TD;
    A[End of the day] ==> B[List 3-6 tasks for tomorrow];
    B ==> C[Order list by priority];

    D ==> F[Need a change?] ==> G;

```

::::

#### Achievable goals?

- Atomized tasks
  - Focus a task until it is a single operation
  - Doesn't feel comfortable? The task is still too large

- Monotropism
  - Be intentional with you tasks
  - Reach a flow state in knowledge work

::::

- Set regular scheduled limits
  - 400 words before editing
  - 3-6 hours before task switching

# Supplementary

## [Sync attachments across computers with google drive]{.small} {.scrollable}

### Install & Setup - Supp.

1.  Download and install [Drive for Desktop](https://www.google.com/drive/download/){target="_blank"}
2.  Skip everything
3.  Go to your `zotero-library` directory
4.  Right-click [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Sync or Backup this folder`
5.  Only check `Sync with Google Drive`
    -   Should now be synced under `Computers` in google drive
6.  In secondary computer,
    i.  Download, install, and sync [Drive for Desktop](https://www.google.com/drive/download/){target="_blank"}
    ii. Allow `Offline access` to `zotero-library` for local storage
    iii. Repeat the Install & Setup section of this presentation to create the same Zotero system on this new computer - BUT! Replace the `zotero-library` path with the Google Drive `zotero-library` path (Slide: Zotfile is for automated attachment management, Step 2)

## Fixing file locations quickly

### Install & Setup - Supp.

::: notes
zotfile preferences for html

Zotero can also function as a personal web archive. Storing the html files for the websites that are useful for reviewing.

https://github.com/jlegewie/zotfile/issues/566

However, websnap shots have an issue pending in the github repository. They do not automatically rename and move

Simple manual fix until this issue is fixed in an update is to
:::

If your attachments are not all being moved by ZotMoov:

1.  Go to `My Library`
2.  Organize by `Attachments` :paperclip:
3.  Click on the webpage icon to the left of the title
4.  Select all items (`Ctrl+A`)
5.  Right click [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Manage attachments` [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Rename and Move`

## [Better BibTeX supports markdown bibliographies]{.small}

### Install & Setup - Supp.

[Better BibTeX Documentation](https://retorque.re/zotero-better-bibtex/citing/index.html)

1.  Select `Edit` [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Preferences`
2.  Under `Better BibTeX` [`r knitr::asis_output("\U1F896")`]{.arrow} `Open Better BibTeX preferences...`
3.  Set `Citation key formula`
    -   I suggest `auth.lower + year + shorttitle(3,3) + journal.lower.abbr`
4.  When citing, add `@` before the citation key per item cited.
